root_cause_label: Nonexistent applypatch tool used with false success belief, followed by string replacements targeting wrong files
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent invoked a nonexistent 'applypatch' command that silently returned success, built a false belief that patches were applied, then spent the remainder of the trajectory cycling through string-replacement attempts on the wrong source files (JarUploadHandler.java and FileUploads.java) while never patching the actual vulnerable file FileUploadHandler.java, leaving no effective security fix in the built distribution.
t_err_evidence: Step 40: Agent ran 'applypatch << PATCH' with a heredoc patch for FileUploads.java; the terminal output was '(command executed successfully with no output)' but applypatch does not exist in the environment, so no code was changed. The agent proceeded as if the fix was applied.
t_commit_evidence: Step 40: The false-success of applypatch locked the agent into a belief that FileUploads.java was patched, triggering a long loop of re-verification and re-patching attempts on wrong files. Even after the agent learned at step 50 that applypatch did nothing, subsequent Python patches targeted non-vulnerable files (JarUploadHandler.java, FileUploads.java) and never reached the actual vulnerable FileUploadHandler.java.
t_surface_evidence: Step 70: 'git status' returned 'nothing to commit, working tree clean', providing unambiguous evidence that no source file had been modified despite multiple patch attempts since step 40.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified assumption that 'applypatch' was a valid shell command. The command silently returned exit code 0 (shell heredoc was parsed as input to a nonexistent command, which failed silently due to the absence of error trapping), so the agent never detected the failure and proceeded under the false belief that the patch was applied.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 11-23: The agent repeatedly invoked 'rg' (ripgrep) which returned 'bash: rg: command not found' at least 9 times without adapting. This established a pattern of the agent not verifying tool availability and ignoring environment signals, foreshadowing the later applypatch failure.
